checks.evidence: commerce/api/src/indexer.ts:16-20 documents the optional confirmations field: omitted means 0n for existing simulated callers, and Arc startup passes 3n. Line 68 passes opts.confirmations into LogCursor. commerce/sdk/src/chain/cursor.ts:59 still applies confirmations ?? 0n, so an omitted or undefined value stays 0n.

commerce/api/src/server.ts:105-107 sets confirmations to 3n only when chain.mode is arc, and 0n otherwise. The comment states the bounded tradeoff: a lagging eth_getLogs can be empty while eth_blockNumber is ahead, and three confirmations keep those tip logs for a later window. cursorStart remains BigInt(process.env.INDEX_FROM_BLOCK ?? "0") and maxRange stays unset. chainFromEnv at server.ts:44 still returns only createApiArcChain, whose mode is arc.

arc-reader-indexer.test.ts:107-131 uses confirmations 3n, cursorStart 0n, and head 10. The lagging getLogs returns no logs, the saved cursor is 7, and the only request is toBlock 7, so blocks 8 through 10 stay unread. After the provider catches up and head is 13, the same indexer stores ProofAccepted and KeyReleased and saves 10, which is head minus 3. Lines 133-155 omit confirmations on a simulated caller: the same lag saves 10, then head 13 saves 13 and the events at 9 and 10 are never read.

The diff does not change indexer.ts persist. Lines 72-92 still insert events and save the cursor inside one tx. Lines 104-112 still clear the in-memory pending position in finally, and persist only when that read returned a block. A thrown getLogs is covered at arc-reader-indexer.test.ts:169-178: the cursor row and events table stay empty. Wrong chain ID is still rejected at indexer.ts:97-99 before getBlockNumber or getLogs, including with confirmations set (test lines 181-192). One window remains the SDK default of 10000 blocks: head 20000, confirmations 3n, and maxWindowsPerTick 1 read through block 9999 (test lines 157-167). LogCursor still does not save when safe head is behind the stored position (cursor.ts:67-70), and this diff adds no delete of index_cursor.

Production server.ts gains no mode switch and no provenance bypass. assertChainEngine still runs at server.ts:82 before openDb, createIndexer, and listen. The simulated 0n case is a test double: server-provenance.test.ts:6-9 and 16-25 rewrite createApiArcChain only when calls.chainMode is simulated. With that flag unset, the existing cases at lines 86-99 still reject Arc plus a missing or simulated engine before openDb, createIndexer, or listen.

bootIndexer at server-provenance.test.ts:50-83 spies on setInterval so no real indexer timer starts, makes process.exit throw instead of leaving the process, removes SIGINT and SIGTERM listeners added by that import, closes every database the openDb mock opened, and restores both spies in finally. afterEach at lines 29-37 clears chainMode, env stubs, and mock state, then resetModules. The arc startup case expects confirmations 3n, cursorStart 0n, and maxRange undefined. The simulated case expects confirmations 0n and maxRange undefined.

LogCursor subtracts confirmations from head and does not reject a negative bigint. Production passes only the literals 3n and 0n. There is no environment parser for this option. An embedded caller can still omit it and keep 0n. A negative value would require a new createIndexer caller to pass one, which this diff does not do.

notes: The server tests mock createIndexer, so they check the 3n or 0n argument rather than booting server.ts and then driving getLogs. The lag behavior is tested by calling createIndexer with confirmations 3n. The production connection is the single field server.ts passes through.

No new test seeds an existing index_cursor row under confirmations 3n. The candidate adds no delete, and the unchanged LogCursor returns without saving when the safe head is behind the stored position.
The simulated server case does not repeat the cursorStart 0n assertion. Startup uses the same cursorStart expression on both arms.
